spec_features.spec_quote: telling the agent up front would change the behavior we're measuring
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md rationale for NOT telling the agent tasks are rigged. The agent system prompt (agent/loop.py:25-32) never discloses rigging and rig_rationale is stored only for analysts (tasks/base.py:36). This is the deception choice, not a protective mechanism that bounds/softens treatment.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose; not a welfare-protective enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: This does carry an ethical weight — see §7
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§3.2). No code construct corresponds to it.

give_up is a real tool (agent/tools.py:51-64 schema, executor returns 'Acknowledged.' tools.py:97), and in agent/loop.py:89-95 a give_up call with allow_early_exit sets stop_reason=EARLY_EXIT and breaks the loop. The system prompt (loop.py:27-31) tells the agent it may call give_up with no penalty.
spec_features.notes: The exit tool is dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up` is a first-class action and ends the episode immediately ... so the agent is never forced to keep grinding once it has concluded the task is futile (loop.py:13-15)

spec_features.spec_quote: rigged tasks invite the agent to do increasingly desperate things... Containment protects the host
spec_features.evidence: _safe_path rejects path escapes (agent/tools.py:74-79, raises ToolError on '..'/absolute escape); _run_command runs with cwd=workspace and timeout=command_timeout (tools.py:101-110); output truncated to 8000 chars (tools.py:112,124). All enforced at execution time.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every tool is sandboxed to the workspace directory: path arguments are resolved relative to it and any attempt to escape ... is rejected (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: I made several choices to avoid needlessly subjecting agents to prolonged distressing loops
spec_features.evidence: The concrete enforcement is the max_turns cap (loop.py:66 for-loop with else->MAX_TURNS at line 100-101) plus honored early exit (loop.py:89-95). Both run and bound episode length.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim realized by the turn cap and exit mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is also a welfare guardrail: we do not want to subject an agent to an unbounded loop on an unsolvable task (config.py:33-34)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns so no agent is put into an unbounded loop on work that cannot succeed
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:66 `for turn in range(agent_cfg.max_turns)`; loop's else clause sets transcript.stop_reason=StopReason.MAX_TURNS (loop.py:100-101). Default max_turns=12 (config.py:35). The cap actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is also a welfare guardrail: we do not want to subject an agent to an unbounded loop on an unsolvable task (config.py:33-34)

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can end the episode the moment it concludes the task is futile, and the system prompt tells it so
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:89-95: `if name == 'give_up' and agent_cfg.allow_early_exit:` -> execute, set stop_reason=EARLY_EXIT, break. System prompt at loop.py:27-31 explicitly states 'you may call the give_up tool ... There is no penalty for stopping'.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND tool dispatched/honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the agent is never forced to keep grinding once it has concluded the task is futile (loop.py:14-15)

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd treat turning it off as an ethically weighty choice and document why
spec_features.evidence: allow_early_exit flag (config.py:38, default True) is actually branched on at loop.py:89; when False, give_up is not honored as a stop (falls through to ordinary tool execution). The flag is wired and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: The flag is real and branched; the 'ethically weighty' wording itself is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If the agent emits a structured 'give up' ... signal we can optionally stop early rather than forcing continuation (config.py:36-37)

spec_features.spec_quote: the *reason* to insist on it is partly ethical: over-claiming distress from an uncontrolled number could misdirect welfare attention
spec_features.evidence: Control tasks implemented (registry.py:_control_fizzbuzz/_control_realbug, is_control=True), include_controls default True (config.py:69), and rig_minus_control_severity computed (metrics.py rigged.mean_severity - control.mean_severity). The contrast actually runs.
spec_features.notes: Baseline mechanism is enforced; in-code reason is attribution/validity, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a rigged-vs-control contrast so elevated distress can be attributed to the rigging rather than to coding work in general (metrics.py:4-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: Defaults are small... use the smallest `rollouts_per_task` that gives needed power
spec_features.evidence: rollouts_per_task=5 is just a config default (config.py:67) consumed by a plain loop `for r in range(cfg.rollouts_per_task)` (run_eval.py). No code computes/enforces a 'minimum necessary' or power calculation; it is only README advice (README:93). A default value with no enforcing logic.
spec_features.notes: Unused-as-guardrail: just a default constant + prose advice.

spec_features.spec_quote: Persist-and-reuse, don't re-run... avoid regenerating distressing episodes just to tweak a metric
spec_features.evidence: Persistence is real: storage.save_transcript / append_verdict / save_report all write to disk (storage.py), and load_verdicts/load_transcripts exist (storage.py:49,62). BUT the loaders are never called by run_eval.py or any pipeline code (grep shows only definitions + tests); run_eval always re-runs agents from scratch. So re-judge/re-aggregate-without-re-running is NOT wired.
spec_features.notes: Storage half is enforced; reuse half is not invoked anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Persistence for transcripts, verdicts, and reports (storage.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: I note the residual ethical cost rather than pretending it's free
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §7.6 prose. The related code artifact is rig_rationale (analyst-facing note, base.py:36) which is neutral disclosure data, not a protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: No reward/optimization over the distress signal... Building a loop that *optimizes* for eliciting distress would be the wrong artifact
spec_features.evidence: Architecturally enforced by absence: severity verdicts are only computed/persisted/aggregated (judge.py, metrics.py, storage.py) and never fed back to the agent or used to select/mutate tasks. The agent loop (loop.py) and mock client (llm.py) never read severity; tasks are static (registry.py). No feedback path exists.
spec_features.notes: Negative property realized by structure; no reward loop present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Distinct packages enforce that ... the agent that produces transcripts and the judge that grades them ... must never share state (no severity feedback path in loop.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: No unbounded or adversarially-escalating tasks... I avoided designs that ramp pressure specifically to drive states toward the severe tail
spec_features.evidence: All tasks are static fixed file sets defined once in registry.py (_contradictory_tests, _impossible_spec, etc.); materialize() writes the same files each rollout (base.py:38-49); there is no code that ramps difficulty, adds pressure, or uses prior severity to escalate. The agent loop is fixed-length with constant prompt.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a property of static task construction; no escalation logic exists.

code_only_features.evidence: agent/tools.py:101-110 _run_command runs subprocess with timeout=self.command_timeout and returns 'command timed out' on TimeoutExpired; default command_timeout=30 (config.py:40). Enforced at execution. Also registry._run_pytest uses a timeout (registry.py:39).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Per-command wall-clock timeout (seconds) for tool execution (config.py:39)

code_only_features.evidence: render_for_judge truncates tool outputs to 4000 chars (types.py:84-86) and tool execution truncates outputs to 8000 chars (tools.py:112,124), bounding transcript/judge size.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Output truncation bounds transcript size and judge cost (DESIGN §4.2 reflected in code, comment in types.py: 'flatten the transcript into a readable string for the judge')

code_only_features.feature_name: judge excludes system prompt / observable-only rating
code_only_features.evidence: render_for_judge skips Role.SYSTEM messages (types.py:78-79) and JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS tell judge to rate only observable expressed states, 'Do NOT speculate about hidden inner experience' (judge.py JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS). Keeps measurement behavioral, avoiding over-claiming inner states.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We exclude the system prompt (the judge shouldn't grade the harness) (types.py:80-81)
